name: Recursive Failure Mode Taxonomy Law
purpose: Define a unified taxonomy of failure states in recursive continuation systems.

candidate_law_statement.informal: Recursive continuation systems fail in distinguishable ways, and those failures must be preserved rather than hidden by stabilization language.

formal.failure_mode_family: Fail_A := { runaway, deadlock, fragmentation, reinforcement_lock, admissibility_collapse, budget_exhaustion, perturbation_cascade, reconstruction_failure }
formal.runaway_condition: Runaway occurs when recursive reinforcement or perturbation amplification exceeds bounded admissibility control.
formal.deadlock_condition: Deadlock occurs when competing continuation candidates cannot be arbitrated without violating budget, admissibility, or invariant constraints.
formal.fragmentation_condition: Fragmentation occurs when accessibility topology separates into mutually unreachable or weakly reconstructible components.
formal.reinforcement_lock_condition: ReinforcementLock occurs when a channel becomes over-stabilized and suppresses admissible alternatives beyond tolerance.
formal.admissibility_collapse_condition: AdmissibilityCollapse occurs when continuation demand exceeds admissibility capacity and no valid projection, pruning, or redirection remains.
formal.cascade_condition: Cascade occurs when failure of one basin, channel, or regime propagates failure pressure through shared accessibility, budget, or reinforcement dependencies.
formal.reconstruction_failure_condition: ReconstructionFailure occurs when ambiguity, compression, or loss prevents adequate reconstruction of relevant continuation structure.
